label: dense near-always-on candidate feature (weaker at first steps)
explanation: Active on ~90% of all steps in every sequence. Rate is lower only at the first original steps (t=0: 53%, t=1: 70%) and rises to ~96% in delimiter/copy phases; copy phase holds ~51% of activation mass. No token, position, or history variable gives lift above ~1.1x. The predicate t>=1 (F1 0.94 dev) does no better than the trivial always-on baseline (F1 0.947), so it is not an explanation. The largest activations (~6) come in copy steps that output a 2 (often followed by c, e.g. ...2 2 c), but outputting 2/c covers under 9% of mass, so it is a magnitude hint and not the identity of the feature.
